Independently researched morphology: Mature medium-sized athletic muscular Banter Bulldogge, distinctly balanced functional legs underneath the body, neither squat nor lanky; body slightly longer than leg height, compact square rear. Square muscular head, mostly flat skull with pronounced stop, muscular cheeks, rounded almond wide-set brown eyes and slightly wrinkled brow. Short broad substantial muzzle with slight undershot jaw, not upturned; balanced black nose with open nostrils. Natural short rose ears. Thick well-muscled high neck blending into strong forelimbs. Deep square chest down to elbows, substantial but not exaggerated width; slight arch over the muscular back. Straight strong defined forelegs, muscular hindquarters with moderate angulation, compact round feet and firm pasterns. Short smooth coat; choose rich red with very small white chest mark and black muzzle shading. Complete high-set natural tail reaching near the top of the hock, relaxed shallow curve, clear attached base and visible free tip; natural length is literal IOEBA and AMA standard, not reconstructed from obscured or docked source photos. Show a relaxed dog-eye-level three-quarter standing pose facing right with head gently turned toward the viewer, believable weight and calm alert expression. Keep entire head, ears, trunk, all four coherent legs and grounded paws, and complete natural attached tail within generous crop-safe margins. Four paws clearly visible on firm ground with natural joints and contact shadows. Separate tail tip visibly from hind legs. Setting: Open firm sandy ground beside a quiet Florida live-oak grove, sparse short grass, warm morning light. profileEvidence.summary: Often playful and attached to their household, Banter Bulldogges can settle indoors while remaining keen on active work and sounding an alarm at intruders. Todd Tripp developed this modern American breed in the late 1990s, inspired by the extinct Brabanter Bullenbeisser. His PullDoggies kennel competes in weight pull, keeping physical working tests central to its breeding.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: Playful and attached to their household, Banter Bulldogges often enjoy active work and sound an alarm at intruders.
